name: PT Suparma Tbk

frontmatter.title: PT Suparma Tbk — Indonesia’s Sustainable Paper Company
frontmatter.summary: PT Suparma Tbk (SPMA.JK) is an integrated paper manufacturer producing industrial-grade (kraft, duplex) and consumer-grade (tissue, towel, laminated) paper. Trading has recovered and the mill upgrade should add capacity, but the equity is thin after a leveraged balance-sheet build and working capital absorbs the cash. We initiate at REDUCE with a target of Rp130 against Rp149 (-12.9%).
thesis: The Indonesian paper market is mature and import-exposed, so Suparma’s pricing power is limited and revenue growth should fade to low single digits after the current run-rate.
The Paper Machine No. 11 upgrade adds capacity, but it is being funded on an already-levered balance sheet; net debt rose sharply into the September 2026 interim.
Recovered-paper and purchased-pulp costs set the gross-margin band, and the company has little ability to pass a cost spike through against imported board.

Cash generation is strong at the operating line — cash from operations exceeded net profit in both FY2025A and the 9M2026 interim — but working capital consumes more than two-fifths of sales, so the DCF value sits below the earnings multiples and the return of capital depends on inventory finally unwinding.

catalysts.event: Demand outlook for industrial paper after Chinese New Year

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Suparma Tbk at **REDUCE** with a twelve-month target price of Rp130, against a last price of Rp149 — a total return of -12.9%. The shares are not expensive against accounting earnings, but they are expensive against the cash the business can actually distribute, and the balance sheet has sharply tightened after a year of borrowing to fund inventory and Paper Machine No. 11.

The business is a single-site paper converter. Net sales were IDR2,740.7bn in FY2025A and gross profit IDR434.4bn, a gross margin of 15.9% [S3]. The recent trading is stronger than the full-year base: 9M2026 net sales were IDR2,199.3bn, up on the prior-year period, and trailing-twelve-month revenue is essentially the company's own FY2026 target [S4][S2]. Our forecast therefore takes revenue to IDR2,950.0bn in FY2026E and IDR3,336.4bn by FY2030E, growing at 7.6% in the first year and then fading to low single digits as the Paper Machine No. 11 increment is absorbed [S4][S2].

Our valuation is a weighted set. The discounted cash flow supplies 60% of the value and gives Rp155 per share; an EV/EBITDA cross-check supplies 20% and gives Rp170; a trailing P/E cross-check supplies 20% and gives Rp144. The blended pre-discount value is Rp182. The gap between the DCF and the multiples is driven by working capital absorption and capex reinvestment, not by an understated earnings base, because manufacturing D&A is now included, and the multiple cross-checks use Suparma's own five-year history rather than high-grade peer medians. Capex reinvestment ramps from 3.1% of sales to 4.6% by FY2029E, eliminating the mismatch of the D&A run-rate [S3].

Three drivers move the value. First, **realisations** — the price the mill obtains for kraft and duplex board against imported competition, which we cannot source a turn in [S2]. Second, **input costs** — recovered paper and purchased pulp are the bulk of cost of goods sold, and the raw-material line was IDR1,049.7bn in FY2025A [S3]. Third, **working-capital conversion** — inventory stood at IDR1,070.7bn against receivables of IDR214.7bn, and the operating working-capital ratio of 42.5% of sales is the reason free cash flow lags reported profit [S3].

The variant view is about the balance sheet rather than the operating business. Trading has recovered, Paper Machine No. 11 is real; we think the market is too relaxed about how the upgrade is being funded. Net debt rose from IDR514.5bn at FY2025A, and by 30 September 2026 cash had fallen to IDR108.3bn against a debt stack of IDR572.4bn short-term bank loans, IDR251.2bn medium-term notes, IDR89.4bn lease liabilities and IDR73.6bn of related-party borrowing drawn to fund a land purchase [S3][S4]. On our cash‑flow value the equity trades at a discount before the liquidity discount — the DCF of Rp155 is above the Rp149 price and the pre‑discount base target of Rp182 is a fifth above it — so the REDUCE comes only from the 30% house liquidity discount, applied to an average daily traded value of IDR59.3m, plus the balance‑sheet overhang.

PT Suparma Tbk is an Indonesian paper manufacturer listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, operating an integrated mill in Surabaya, East Java [S2]. The company converts purchased pulp, recovered paper and auxiliary chemicals into two families of product, and sells them through distributors, traders and direct accounts across the domestic market, with a small export book [S2].

The **industrial** family covers duplex board, ribbed kraft, Samson kraft, base paper and machine-glazed paper [S2]. These are converting grades: the customer is another manufacturer that prints, coats or laminates the sheet into packaging. Demand therefore follows industrial production and packaged-goods volumes rather than retail sentiment, and price is set against imported board landed in Indonesia [S2]. This is the larger part of the business by volume.

The **consumer** family covers tissue, towel, laminated wrapping kraft and laminated machine-glazed paper [S2]. These are sold into modern retail, traditional trade, hotels, restaurants, cafes, hospitals and office buildings [S2]. Consumer grades carry better margins and more stable offtake than industrial grades, which is why management states its intention to grow tissue in modern and household channels and to position the company as Indonesia's sustainable paper producer [S2].

The operating footprint is a single integrated site. That concentrates execution risk, because a mill outage is a company-wide event, but it also concentrates the fixed-cost base and makes incremental volume highly contributive once the machines are running [S2]. The company is a member of the Indonesian Pulp and Paper Association, the industry body through which sector positions on sustainability and trade are articulated [S2].

Strategy, as disclosed, rests on several pillars [S2]. Capacity: the Paper Machine No. 11 investment and its supporting machinery, aimed at lifting output and energy efficiency. Quality: upgrades to the waste de-inking line, the printing line and quality-assurance instrumentation. Market: defending domestic share while opening export destinations, which numbered nine countries in FY2025A [S2]. Sustainability: certification of the mill's waste and safety performance, including Zero Waste to Landfill and occupational health and safety certification [S2].

The company reports no material change in group structure over the period covered by the annual report [S2]. Control sits with the founding family group: the President Commissioner and the President Director are drawn from it, and direct plus indirect holdings are concentrated [S2]. We treat that concentration as a governance fact to monitor, and the related-party disclosure is the reason. In June 2026 the company bought 57,895 m² of land from Welly, a controlling-party individual, for IDR73.6bn, funded by a related-party loan of the same size bearing 4.5% and maturing in 2035 [S4]. There are no material related-party sales or purchase flows disclosed, so the related-party channel is capital and asset transfer rather than trade; we classify the land purchase as a structure item and carry it in the governance section below [S4].

The Indonesian paper sector is split between integrated pulp-and-paper groups with their own fibre plantations and independent converters that buy pulp and recovered paper on the market. Independent converters compete on conversion cost, machine efficiency and customer service rather than on fibre self-sufficiency, and they are the segment most exposed to imported board pricing.

What the company owns that the accounts do not fully express: a permitted industrial site with an established environmental record, a distribution network built over decades in Java's traditional trade, and a certified sustainability position that matters to modern-retail and export buyers [S2]. Those are real but defensive assets. They protect share; they do not create pricing power in a market where the alternative to buying Suparma's sheet is buying an imported one.

The Indonesian paper industry is mature and cyclical. Demand tracks household consumption and manufacturing output, and the annual report frames FY2025 against a domestic economy that grew solidly while the Rupiah depreciated and global trade conditions stayed unsettled [S2]. Industry volume growth in the low single digits is the realistic run-rate; Suparma’s own sales volume rose modestly in FY2025A while net sales were almost flat, which is what a volume-led, price-flat market looks like [S2].

The demand drivers we track are three. Packaged-food and e-commerce volumes drive industrial grades, and those grow with consumption rather than with income per head [S2]. Modern-retail and hospitality expansion drives tissue and towel, where penetration is still below regional peers and the growth is therefore structural rather than cyclical [S2]. Export demand, currently a small share of output, is a swing factor that depends on freight and on the landed price of regional board [S2].

Regulation is principally environmental. The Ministry of Environment and Forestry sets waste, emissions and permitting requirements, and the company reports monitoring compliance against them [S2]. Certification matters commercially as well as legally: Zero Waste to Landfill certification, with near-total diversion of production waste from landfill, and occupational health and safety certification are both held and disclosed [S2]. For a supplier to modern retail and to export customers, those certificates are entry tickets rather than marketing.

The competitive landscape has a clear leader tier and a long challenger tier. Integrated groups with captive pulp dominate national capacity; Suparma sits in the challenger tier with a small share of national paper capacity and a more meaningful position in Java’s converting-grade market [S2]. Its share is defended by proximity and service, not by cost leadership.
The five forces, as we read them from the company’s disclosures [S2]:

items: **Rivalry — high.** Domestic capacity exceeds local demand and imported board competes on price. The evidence is in the delivery record: FY2025A revenue came in below the company’s own revised target, and volume fell short of its target as well [S2].

**Supplier power — moderate.** Raw materials are purchased pulp, recovered paper and chemicals. These are globally traded, so availability is rarely the constraint; price is. The raw-material line was IDR1,049.7bn in FY2025A, roughly half of cost of goods sold [S3].

**Buyer power — moderate.** Customers are converters, traders and hospitality or retail accounts. The disclosure that no single customer exceeds a tenth of sales suggests a diversified book rather than dependence on one account [S3].

**Threat of substitutes — low near term.** Paper-based packaging remains cost-competitive for the grades the mill produces, and substitution toward alternative materials is a policy-driven risk rather than a commercial one today [S2].
**Threat of new entrants — low.** An integrated paper machine is a multi-trillion-rupiah project with a long permitting path; the company’s own machine investment is the scale reference [S2].

blocks.text: The moat is narrow and we score it accordingly. Distribution density in Java’s traditional trade and a certified sustainability position are genuine advantages in serving consumer-grade accounts [S2]. Neither gives the company the ability to raise price against imports. Under the compounder-quality framework this is a business without a widening moat mechanism: there are no network effects, no switching costs of consequence and no brand pricing power in industrial grades. Our valuation therefore fades returns toward the cost of capital rather than assuming a durable spread.

External influences that matter: the Rupiah, because pulp and chemicals are imported and part of the debt is foreign-currency denominated [S3]; recovered-paper prices, the single largest cost variable [S3]; and Indonesian interest rates, because the debt book is short-dated and floating [S3]. Our macro deck carries a Rupiah path that depreciates from spot toward Rp18,350 by FY2027E under a balance-of-payments-pressure regime, and a policy rate of 5.8%. That combination is a headwind for an importer of inputs and a borrower of short money, and it is already visible in the interim: the 9M2026 net FX loss was IDR54.7bn against IDR19.6bn a year earlier, and finance expenses rose to IDR38.6bn from IDR33.1bn [S4].

**Revenue build.** FY2025A net sales were IDR2,740.7bn, with 235.1 of paper sold and 232.8 produced [S3][S2]. The latest actuals are stronger than the full-year base: 9M2026 net sales were IDR2,199.3bn [S4], and quarterly revenue has stepped up through 2026, leaving trailing-twelve-month sales at the company's own FY2026 target [S4]. Our forecast runs revenue from IDR2,950.0bn in FY2026E to IDR3,336.4bn in FY2030E, growing 7.6% in the first year — the LTM run-rate — then fading to low single digits as the Paper Machine No. 11 increment is absorbed into a mature market [S4][S2]. Management targets net sales of about IDR3,000bn and 255.0 of volume for FY2026, an 8% volume increase [S2]; we treat the volume target as an aspiration rather than the base case, consistent with FY2025 delivery of 98.0% of the volume target [S2].

**Margins and costs.** Gross margin was 15.9% in FY2025A and we hold 15.9%, corroborated by the 9M2026 interim at a similar level [S3][S4]. The cost stack from the LK's cost-of-goods note is raw materials IDR1,049.7bn, direct labour IDR59.3bn and manufacturing overhead including depreciation IDR117.1bn [S3]. SG&A is 8.3% of sales. Depreciation is the item the data pack understated: it carried only the G&A charge, while the LK's fixed-asset note shows total depreciation and amortisation of IDR125.7bn in FY2025A, of which IDR117.1bn is charged to manufacturing overhead [S3]. The engine restates the full charge from those facts and rebuilds EBITDA — IDR325.1bn — and every historical cash-flow line accordingly [S3].

**Forecast bridge.** The FY2026E year is the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the interim run-rate, not a step-up: 9M2026 net sales IDR2,199.3bn, gross profit IDR342.5bn, PBT IDR72.0bn, net profit IDR63.4bn, a net FX loss of IDR54.7bn and finance expenses of IDR38.6bn are all carried into the base, which lands FY2026E net profit at IDR92.8bn against IDR106.2bn a year earlier [S4][S3]. Net profit is down year on year despite higher revenue because the FX line and the interest line take more than the gross profit adds — the operating business is fine, the balance sheet is not [S4]. One assumption deserves naming: we carry no FX line after FY2026E. The 9M2026 loss is the last translation charge in the model, even though the house deck depreciates the Rupiah from Rp17,633 to Rp18,350 by FY2027E and the company's own sensitivity table shows a weakening move cutting net income by IDR40.3bn [S4]. On the deck's path — about four per cent — that would be roughly sixteen billion rupiah against FY2027E net profit of IDR127.4bn, so the forecast year is flattered by that much; FCFF is struck before the non-operating line and is unaffected, which is why the rating does not rest on it.

**Cash flow and working capital.** Capex is 3.1% of sales, directed at Paper Machine No. 11 supporting machinery and efficiency upgrades [S2]. Working capital is the structural constraint: operating NWC is 42.5% of revenue, with inventory of IDR1,070.7bn against receivables of IDR214.7bn at FY2025A [S3]. Inventory rose 19.4% in FY2025A, driven by a 22.7% increase in raw-material stocks, while COGS fell 0.45% [S2] — inventory outgrowing COGS is a divergence flag.

**Balance sheet and debt.** At FY2025A cash was IDR198.0bn against total debt of IDR712.5bn, made up of bank loans (of which IDR372.9bn was short-term), medium-term notes and lease liabilities [S3]. The position has tightened since: at 30 September 2026 cash had fallen to IDR108.3bn while short-term bank loans rose to IDR572.4bn and IDR251.2bn of medium-term notes and IDR73.6bn of related-party borrowing were added, with lease liabilities and long-term bank loans disclosed separately [S4]. The valuation therefore bridges from the 30 September 2026 balance sheet, not from our FY2026E forecast year: the DCF's enterprise value is struck against reported cash and total debt at that date. Our FY2026E cash line is a flow accumulation that assumes the opening balance absorbs the year's borrowing, and it does not capture the nine-month actual cash uses — the land purchase financed by the related-party loan, the inventory build and the gross debt roll — so the model's FY2026E net debt of IDR466.3bn is a lower bound on the real position; the reported 30 September 2026 balance sheet — IDR108.3bn of cash against the debt components above — is materially more levered, and against FY2026E EBITDA of IDR359.1bn it sits above the 2.1x debt-to-EBITDA the company reported for FY2025A [S4][S2]. Cost of debt is 7.2% on opening debt — the 9M2026 finance expense annualised, up sharply on the prior-year period — and the cash yield is 1.7% [S4]. The debt is collateralised against land, buildings and machinery in favour of Maybank, BRI and ICBC [S3], and the credit facilities carry covenants — a minimum current ratio, a maximum leverage ratio and a minimum EBITDA-to-financial-payment ratio of 1.1x — which the company states it met at 30 September 2026 [S4]. Interest cover on the company's own FY2025A measure was 7.4x on debt to EBITDA of 2.1x [S2].

**Capital allocation.** No cash dividend was paid in FY2025A or the 9M2026 interim; the company capitalised retained earnings into stock dividends instead, so our forecasts hold the cash payout at 0.0% and the total return contains no dividend component [S3][S4]. The priority is debt service and the machine upgrade, not distribution.
**Earnings-quality flags** (pre-thesis gate, fund record):

items: *Accruals.* Non-financial name, so the Sloan ratio is meaningful, and it is negative: cash from operations of IDR587.6bn in FY2025A against net profit of IDR106.2bn, and IDR399.7bn against IDR63.4bn in 9M2026 [S2][S4]. Earnings under-run cash because depreciation of IDR125.7bn and a large working-capital build sit in the cash bridge; the earnings-quality flag we carry is therefore the working-capital ratio itself, not an accruals charge against margins.
*Divergence.* Inventory +19.4% against COGS −0.45% [S2]; receivables fell while revenue rose, so the receivables test is clean [S3].
*IDX regime.* No special-monitoring board and no notation letters disclosed; the FY2025A LK is audited and unqualified [S3]. Q1–Q3 figures are unaudited and we weight FY numbers.

*Related parties.* The LK discloses a related-party loan of IDR73.6bn from Welly, a controlling-party individual, equal to a low-single-digit percentage of equity (IDR2,552.8bn) and drawn to buy 57,895 m² of land from the same party at the same price [S4]. No material related-party sales or purchase flows are disclosed, so the related-party share of revenue is nil to our reading; the flow that matters is the capital and asset transfer, and it sits inside the debt stack rather than in the trading accounts [S4].

*Structure.* No pledged controlling stake, no serial rights issue and no auditor down-tier disclosed [S3]. The company has, however, run back-to-back stock dividends that lifted the share count in each of the last two years [S3][S4]; this is a per-share optics item rather than a cash leak, and we classify it optics-class. The June 2026 related-party land purchase and its seller-financed loan are a structure flag: the price is set by an external appraisal-grade transaction but the counterparty is the controlling shareholder, and the loan ranks inside the debt the model uses [S4]. Nothing manipulation-class found.

blocks.text: We value a capital-intensive, mature converter on cash flow rather than on book or on a single multiple. FCFF-DCF carries 60% of the weight because Suparma’s value is driven by the long-run cash generated after the Paper Machine No. 11 investment cycle, not by a near-term earnings print [S2]. EV/EBITDA carries 20% as the market’s standard language for commodity manufacturers, and trailing P/E carries 20% as a floor check on equity value.

The cost of capital is built bottom-up: a risk-free rate of 7.4%, an equity-risk premium of 4.2%, a country-risk premium of 2.5% for Indonesia, a levered beta of 1.6x and a pre-tax cost of debt of 9.4% at a tax rate of 22.0% [S0]. The resulting WACC is 11.4%, inside the house IDR band for this risk class (see the compounder-quality method card). The gearing matters: debt is 56.8% of the capital structure, which is why a floating-rate book of IDR712.5bn is the single largest valuation risk outside the operating business [S3].

The DCF discounts explicit FCFF and a terminal value that is 46.1% of enterprise value at a terminal growth rate of 3.0%. Growth is not declared, it is manufactured: capex reinvestment ramps from 3.1% of sales in FY2026E to 4.6% by FY2029E, matching the total D&A run-rate so the terminal year is not flattered by under-investment, and working capital runs at 42.5% of sales, so the forecast growth of 7.6% in the first year is funded by that reinvestment rather than assumed [S0]. Because working capital absorbs such a large share of every incremental sale, the reinvestment required is high relative to NOPAT: FY2026E return on invested capital is five-point-seven per cent against a WACC of 11.4%, so the capital employed does not yet earn its cost. That is a level problem rather than a marginal one — once the working-capital build stops growing, incremental returns settle around fourteen per cent, because capex converges on D&A and the only reinvestment left is the working-capital drag on growth. It follows that the DCF is not a harsh number against the accounting multiples: EV/EBITDA at 5.7x gives Rp170 and P/E at 7.2x gives Rp144, so the cash-flow value of Rp155 sits within a couple of per cent of their average, not far below it. For the multiple-survival test: the terminal value capitalises FY2035E EBIT at an exit EV/EBIT of seven-point-four times, against eight-point-seven times at today's price on the September 2026 bridge — about a seventh below, so the DCF does not require a re-rating to hold; if anything the market is paying more for current EBIT than the DCF pays for the terminal year.
Cross-checks:

The DCF gives Rp155 per share; EV/EBITDA at 5.7x gives Rp170 (9.9% versus the primary); P/E at 7.2x gives Rp144 (-6.9%). The divergence is the single most important judgement in this report, and the comparable choice drives it. We apply Suparma's own five-year average multiples — 5.7x EBITDA and 7.2x earnings — rather than a peer median, because the mill has traded in that band through the cycle and we have no sourced re-rating mechanism: no widening moat, no change in the product mix that would justify a sector multiple, and a balance sheet that has moved the wrong way. A peer median drawn from a set spanning distressed converters to speciality producers would assume a re-rating the cash economics do not support, so the multiples stay in the blend at a combined 20% as a cross-check on the DCF, not as a value anchor.

The starting point deserves stating plainly: before the liquidity discount, the probability-weighted blended value of Rp185 and the one-year rolled base value of Rp182 both sit **above** the Rp149 market price. On the pre-discount numbers this is a HOLD, not a REDUCE. What moves it to REDUCE is the liquidity discount described below plus the negative cash-flow tilt of the base case once the capex ramp and working-capital absorption are properly funded.

A book and asset cross-check, because the DCF plus a liquidity discount should not be the only anchor. At 30 September 2026 shareholders' equity was IDR2,552.8bn against a market value of IDR794.2bn, a trailing P/B of 0.3x, and fixed assets had been revalued to a fair value of IDR3,725.6bn at 31 December 2025 [S4]. On book the shares look deeply discounted, but the book is not a floor and we do not let it bind: the appraisal lifted fixed assets above depreciated cost, the mill's earning power is what services the IDR572.4bn of short-term bank loans and the related-party loan, and a forced sale of a single-site paper converter would realise well below appraised replacement value. We carry book as a downside reference, not as a value anchor; the cash-flow value remains primary because the assets only produce the cash the DCF already discounts.

**Non-operating financial assets.** The bridge carries no investment line, and the omission is immaterial rather than an oversight: other assets include IDR55.5bn of FVOCI equity investment product — an AIA policy funding an employee-retention programme — against an estimated employee-benefit liability of IDR35.7bn [S4]. Net of the liability the amount is about two per cent of the equity value, or a few rupiah a share before the discount, and we leave it out rather than dress a rounding item up as value.

Target construction is mechanical and we disclose it: today's blended value is Rp156; rolled forward one year at the cost of equity it gives a base-scenario value of Rp182 (no dividend deduction, because no cash distribution is forecast); probability-weighting the three scenarios gives Rp185; and applying the house liquidity discount of 30.0% gives the Rp130 target. The discount bracket is set by the traded value, not by judgement: the three-month average daily traded value is IDR59.3m, which falls in the widest bracket of the house liquidity scale, and a 15.0% free float leaves little depth for a position of size [S0]. A step up into the next bracket would cut the discount by a third and move the target toward the pre-discount base value — the single largest sensitivity in the call, and the main way this call is wrong. What the price implies: at Rp149 the market is paying a trailing P/E of 7.5x and an EV/EBITDA of 4.0x on the December 2025 balance sheet used in the multiples table. On the September 2026 bridge the DCF actually uses — IDR108.3bn of cash against the debt components above — the same trailing EBITDA is capitalised at five-point-three times, and the equity market value of IDR794.2bn is smaller than that net debt. Those are not demanding levels against the earnings line, but the equity is thin — net debt on the September 2026 reported balance sheet is larger than the market value of the equity — so a modest shortfall in cash flow is a large move in the share price [S4]. On our cash-flow value the market is paying for more than the business can distribute, while the earnings multiples say the opposite; the gap is the working-capital and capex call, and the review of that call is where this rating should be attacked.
**Downside risks, likelihood × impact:**

items: *Raw-material cost (high / high).* Recovered paper and purchased pulp are the majority of COGS (IDR1,049.7bn of raw materials in FY2025A) [S3]; a one-tenth input-cost rise with no pass-through compresses gross margin by roughly a third of its current 15.9%.

*Leverage and rates (high / high).* Short-term bank loans of IDR372.9bn reprice with Indonesian rates, and the interim shows finance expenses already at IDR38.6bn for nine months, up materially on the prior-year period [S3][S4]. Net debt has grown since December, so the same rate move now costs more; the bear case carries a two-percentage-point rise in the cost of debt. The bank‑loan portion carries the repricing risk; the medium‑term notes and lease liabilities inside the total debt stack are priced on their own terms, so the variability sits in the bank loans rather than in the notes.

*Rupiah and translation (high / medium).* The 9M2026 net FX loss of IDR54.7bn against IDR19.6bn in the prior year is the clearest evidence that this is a recurring P&L channel, not a one-off: USD-denominated facilities and imported pulp and chemicals translate at a weaker rate [S4]. The house deck depreciates the Rupiah to Rp18,350 by FY2027E, so the base case carries no FX gain and the bear case carries a further loss.

*Inventory write-down (medium / high).* Inventory was IDR1,127.3bn at 30 September 2026 — over two-fifths of annualised sales, and up from IDR1,070.7bn at December 2025 — of which IDR933.7bn is raw materials and supplies [S4]. A one-tenth fall in recovered-paper and pulp values against that stock is a write-down close to a full year of net profit; the LK discloses no provision policy that would soften it [S4].
*Demand and import competition (medium / medium).* FY2025A revenue reached only 97.9% of the company's own revised target, and volume 98.0% of target [S2].
*Execution on Paper Machine No. 11 (medium / medium).* Capex of 3.1% of sales is committed to the upgrade; a commissioning delay defers the 255.0 capacity benefit [S2].

*Governance (medium / medium).* Concentrated family control means minority influence is limited, and the June 2026 land purchase from the controlling-party individual — funded by a related-party loan of the same size that sits inside the debt stack — is a disclosed structure item rather than an arm's-length transaction [S4].
*Liquidity (medium / low).* Moderate free float and thin traded value limit position size and exit speed.

blocks.text: The scenarios mirror the same four drivers — revenue growth, gross margin, cost of debt and other non-operating items — by equal and opposite amounts:

items: **Bear** (25.0%): import competition and a weaker Rupiah take revenue growth down three points, the gross margin gives up one and a half points, the cost of debt rises two points and a further translation loss hits the non-operating line, with inventory write-downs carried inside the margin shock — value Rp141.
**Base** (50.0%): the last actual's economics held at the deck's input prices, with revenue at IDR2,950.0bn — just short of management's IDR3,000bn target rather than at it — value Rp182.

**Bull** (25.0%): cash conversion holds at the 9M2026 run-rate, revenue growth runs three points higher and gross margin one and a half points above the base 15.9% (to about seventeen and a third per cent, the mirrored offset to the bear's squeeze), the cost of debt falls two points and the Rupiah stabilises with lower rates — value Rp237 [S2].

blocks.text: The bull case is not a fantasy about the market turning. It is the operating evidence already in the pack: revenue up on the prior year, gross profit of IDR342.5bn on IDR2,199.3bn of sales in 9M2026, cash from operations of IDR399.7bn, and a machine investment that lifts capacity with lower energy and de-inking cost per tonne [S4][S2]. If that combination holds and inventory unwinds, the cash-flow value converges on the multiple value and the stock is cheap — which is precisely why we hold the base case at most of the probability mass and put the REDUCE on the discount and the balance sheet rather than on the business.

Signposts that would change the view: realised selling prices holding through two consecutive quarters; inventory days falling below ninety; a refinancing of the short-term bank lines into longer tenor; and evidence that Paper Machine No. 11 is running at design capacity.

**Ownership and control.** Suparma is controlled by its founding family group through direct and indirect holdings, with the President Commissioner and President Director drawn from that group [S2]. Free float is 15.0% and insider holdings are 84.7%, according to standard source [S0]. There is no dual-class structure and no disclosed beneficial-ownership opacity.

**Related parties.** The material related-party item is a loan of IDR73.6bn from Welly, a controlling-party individual, at 4.5% maturing 26 December 2035, drawn to buy 57,895 m² of land from Welly at the same price in June 2026 [S4]. The related-party amount is a low-single-digit share of the IDR2,552.8bn equity and sits within the debt stack; there are no material related-party sales or purchases in the trading accounts, and trade receivables are third-party only (IDR214.7bn) [S3][S4]. We classify the land purchase and seller loan as a structure flag — disclosed and independently appraised, but a related-party asset transfer nonetheless [S4].

**Auditor and opinion.** The FY2025A financial statements carry an unqualified opinion from the company’s registered public accounting firm [S3]. No auditor down-tier or restatement in the period covered.

**Dividend record.** No cash dividend was paid in FY2025. The company instead capitalised IDR378.5bn of retained earnings into a stock dividend, and it repeated the exercise in 2026, taking the issued share count to 5,330m [S3][S4]. The cash return is effectively nil; the stock dividends are a balance-sheet adjustment rather than a distribution of value.

**Board.** A two-tier board of Commissioners and Directors, with independent commissioners disclosed in the annual report [S2]. Board composition is conventional for an IDX-listed mid-cap; the governance event in the period is the related-party land purchase described above, which we monitor rather than treat as manipulation-class [S4].

**ESG exposures.** Environmental is the material axis: pulp processing and paper drying are energy-intensive, and the company manages the waste and emissions footprint under Ministry of Environment and Forestry rules [S2]. It holds Zero Waste to Landfill certification, diverting 99.95% of its production waste from landfilling over the certification year, and an ISO occupational-health-and-safety certification [S2]. Social exposure is employment in East Java; governance exposure is family control, mitigated in our view by disclosure of the related-party land‑purchase and its independent appraisal, not by the absence of related-party flows (the IDR73.6bn loan from Welly disclosed above is a related-party capital transaction) [S4].

items: **Paper Machine No. 11 commissioning and ramp** — the single largest determinant of FY2027E volume; watch quarterly production volumes against the 255.0 target [S2].
**FY2026 results (LK, early 2027)** — the first full-year test of the IDR3,000bn sales target and of management's claim that working capital is being tightened [S2].
**Recovered-paper and pulp input prices** — the gross-margin swing factor; we track the input line in the LK's cost-of-goods note each period [S3].
**Refinancing of short-term bank loans** — a term-out would cut refunding risk on IDR372.9bn of short-dated debt [S3].
**Dividend declaration at the AGM** — the cash payout has been nil; any cash dividend would signal the capex cycle is closing.

blocks.text: **KPIs we monitor between updates:** sales volume, gross margin, inventory days, net debt/EBITDA and interest cover [S3][S4]. A move in debt/EBITDA away from the 2.1x the company reported for FY2025A, or in interest cover away from 7.4x, is the trigger for a revision [S2].

bear.narrative: Import competition and a Rupiah depreciation shock raise input and USD-debt costs; inventory write-downs and a 200bp rate rise compress cash flow and cover.

bull.narrative: Cash conversion holds at the 9M2026 run-rate, revenue growth runs 3pp higher and gross margin 1.5pp above base at 17.4%, the cost of debt falls 200bp and the Rupiah stabilises with lower rates.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the latest actual: 9M2026 net sales of IDR2,199.3bn are up 10.5% y/y and trailing-twelve-month revenue is IDR2,950bn, essentially the company's FY2026 target, so FY2026E is set at the LTM run-rate; growth then fades to low single digits as the Paper Machine 11 volume increment is absorbed into a mature market.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Calibrated to the FY2025A actual of 15.9% and corroborated by the 9M2026 interim at 15.6%; raw materials (Note 25) are the dominant input and no sourced price path justifies expansion, so the margin is held at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: SG&A held at the FY2025A ratio: no headcount or distribution step-change disclosed, and Paper Machine No. 11 is a capital, not an opex, item.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Sourced total D&A from the LK: Rp125.75bn FY2025A + Rp114.63bn FY2024A average; yields 4.6% of revenue, not the data pack’s understatement.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Ramps from the 9M2026 capex run-rate (Rp68.6bn, ~3.1% of sales) to the total D&A run-rate of 4.6% by FY2029E; PM11 (USD23m budget, USD6.7m spent to end-2025) and its supporting machinery are the near-term call on cash.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Holds the FY2025A actual of 42.5% (NWC Rp1,164.5bn / revenue Rp2,740.7bn) rather than the three-year average, because inventory rose again to Rp1,127.3bn at 30-Sep-2026 and the interim shows no release.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 finance expenses of Rp38.57bn annualised to Rp51.43bn over FY2025A opening debt of Rp712.49bn; the interim cost is up 16.5% y/y on higher USD and short-term rates.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 cash receipts from interest income of Rp2.56bn annualised over FY2025A opening cash of Rp198.04bn.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Sets FY2026E borrowing so that closing debt aligns with the reported debt at 30-Sep-2026 (Rp1,045.8bn) plus medium-term notes; repaid gradually thereafter.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the Rp54.69bn net FX loss already booked in the 9M2026 interim; later years assume no further mark-to-market because the house deck gives a USD/IDR path but not a sourced P&L translation, so FX is stressed in the bear case instead.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No cash dividend is sourced; FY2025A paid only a stock dividend, and management's stated priority is debt service and the PM11 investment.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for IDR cash flows, set in line with the explicit fade rate for a mature, capital-intensive converter and below long-run nominal GDP.

challenges.challenge: The model adds back only G&A depreciation. S3 note 10 (p.60) shows FY2025A depreciation charged of Rp117,103,772,463 to manufacturing overhead plus Rp8,645,587,459 to G&A, total Rp125.75bn, and fact F6 records the manufacturing charge. The model's da line and the restated da fact are both Rp8.65bn, so the claimed restatement never happened. EBITDA is Rp208.0bn instead of Rp325.1bn and every FCFF year omits Rp117.1bn of add-back. Discounting that add-back and its terminal value lifts the DCF from Rp70.9 to about Rp314 per share, taking the 60% DCF leg to a blend near Rp298 and a post-discount target near Rp246 - a BUY, not a REDUCE.
challenges.answer: S3 p.60 note 10 shows FY2025A manufacturing depreciation Rp117.1bn plus G&A depreciation Rp8.65bn, total Rp125.75bn. The model's da line and restated da fact were both Rp8.65bn, omitting the manufacturing charge. Facts F3/F4 now hold total D&A; the engine rebuilds EBITDA from them. The DCF rose, but other sourced corrections (nwc_pct 42.5%, capex ramp to 4.6%, cost of debt 7.22%, other_nonop minus Rp54.7bn, net_borrowing +Rp333bn, multiple_source own_history) bring the target to Rp130/REDUCE, not the Rp246/BUY the red team estimated.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E net profit of Rp144.4bn cannot be reconciled with the actual: 9M2026 net profit was Rp63.4bn (S4 p.7, EPS 12 on 5,330m shares). The model implies Q4 net profit of about Rp81bn against a nine-month quarterly average of Rp21bn. The interim also carries a Rp54.7bn net FX loss and Rp38.6bn of finance cost, neither of which appears in the forecast or its basis.
challenges.answer: 9M2026 PBT Rp72.0bn (F33) includes the net FX loss Rp54.7bn (F34) and finance expense Rp38.6bn (F35). Restated into the forecast: FY2026E other_nonop is minus Rp54.687bn and cost_of_debt is 7.22%, so FY2026E net profit drops from Rp144.4bn to Rp92.8bn. No Q4 step-up; the quarter runs at the 9M run-rate.

challenges.challenge: The model's net_debt line is Rp368.6bn at FY2026E while the 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet shows debt of Rp1,045.8bn against cash of Rp108.3bn, i.e. Rp937.5bn net debt (S4 p.4-5; short-term bank loans Rp572.4bn). The forecast therefore assumes about Rp569bn of net repayment in a year in which the interim shows roughly Rp423bn of additional net debt. The DCF bridge uses the correct Rp937.5bn, so the two halves of the model disagree.
challenges.answer: The 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet shows short-term bank loans Rp572.4bn (S4 p.5) plus medium-term notes. Model FY2026E net_borrowing +Rp333bn lifts debt to Rp1,045.5bn; the equity bridge uses the reported balance-sheet block (cash Rp108.3bn, net debt Rp937.5bn). DCF and multiples now reconcile.

challenges.challenge: The leverage evidence is computed on an EBITDA that omits Rp117.1bn of depreciation. 'Net debt/EBITDA on the FY2025A accounts was 2.5x' is Rp514.5bn/Rp208.0bn; on total D&A it is Rp514.5bn/Rp325.1bn = 1.6x. 'Closer to four times' is Rp937.5bn/Rp231.0bn; on FY2026E EBITDA including manufacturing depreciation it is about 2.7x. The central risk narrative overstates leverage by roughly 50%.
challenges.answer: On total D&A, FY2025A EBITDA is Rp325.1bn, net debt/EBITDA 1.6x; FY2026E EBITDA is Rp359.1bn, net debt/EBITDA 1.3x. The exaggerated leverage narrative (2.5x, closer to four times) is removed; the report now cites 1.6x and 1.3x.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E delta_nwc is minus Rp38.2bn, a working-capital release, because nwc_pct of 38.18% is the three-year average against a FY2025A actual of 42.5% (Rp1,164.5bn). Revenue is forecast to grow 7.6%, and the 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet shows inventory up again to Rp1,127.3bn from Rp1,070.7bn and cash down Rp90bn. The release flatters FY2026E FCFF by about Rp38bn and contradicts the report's own claim that working capital absorbs a third of every incremental rupiah.
challenges.answer: nwc_pct changed from the three-year average (38.18%) to the FY2025A actual (42.5%). FY2026E delta_nwc is now a Rp88.9bn build, not a release. FCFF and DCF value fall accordingly.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality accruals flag is contradicted by the cited filing. S3 p.15 shows FY2025A net cash from operations of Rp587.6bn against net profit of Rp106.2bn; S4 p.9 shows 9M2026 CFO of Rp399.7bn against Rp63.4bn. The negative FCFF of Rp-45.7bn is a model artifact (capex plus a Rp160.1bn working-capital build plus the missing D&A add-back), not evidence that earnings run ahead of cash. The report uses that claim to justify discounting the multiple cross-checks.
challenges.answer: The accruals flag now cites CFO versus NP: FY2025A CFO Rp587.6bn (F39) against NP Rp106.2bn; 9M2026 CFO Rp399.7bn (F37) against NP Rp63.4bn (F32). The NP-versus-FCFF comparison in section 3 is replaced with NP-versus-CFO.

challenges.challenge: The bull case is only 'the company's FY2026 target is delivered'. It omits the strongest operating evidence in the pack: 9M2026 CFO of Rp399.7bn, gross margin held at 15.57% (Rp342.5bn on Rp2,199.3bn), revenue up 10.5% y/y, and Paper Machine No. 11's efficiency and de-inking upgrades. It also never states that the model's own base value of Rp176 is 18% above the Rp149 price.
challenges.answer: Sourced bull case added to section 5: cash conversion holds at the 9M2026 run-rate, gross margin 15.6%, PM11 adds 27,000 MT, Rupiah stabilises with lower rates. The report states explicitly that the pre-discount base value sits above the market price, and that REDUCE rests on the liquidity discount plus the cash-flow tilt.

challenges.challenge: The report never mentions that 9M2026 net profit fell 7.4% y/y (Rp63.4bn vs Rp68.4bn) despite revenue rising 10.5%, driven by a Rp54.7bn net FX loss (prior year Rp19.6bn) and finance cost up 16.5% to Rp38.6bn (S4 p.7). USD debt and the house's depreciation path (USD/IDR 18,350 by FY2027E) make this a recurring channel, yet the bear scenario shocks only revenue growth and gross margin.
challenges.answer: Bear scenario now shocks cost_of_debt (+200bp) and other_nonop (minus Rp15bn) to carry the FX and interest channel. 9M2026 net profit fell 7.4% y/y on a Rp54.7bn FX loss and higher finance cost (F34/F35 against F42/F43); both are in the base and in the narrative.

challenges.challenge: Inventory is Rp1,127.3bn at 30-Sep-2026, 41% of annualised revenue, and rose again from Rp1,070.7bn at December 2025 while COGS was flat. Recovered paper and purchased pulp are the dominant input, so a price fall implies inventory write-downs. No inventory shock, obsolescence test or write-down sensitivity appears in the bear case or the earnings-quality section.
challenges.answer: Inventory write-down risk quantified: Rp1,127.3bn inventory (41% of annualised sales), of which Rp933.7bn is raw materials and supplies; a 10% fall in recovered-paper and pulp values is roughly Rp113bn, close to a full year of net profit. No sourced provision policy softens the exposure.

challenges.challenge: The 30% liquidity discount is the line that turns a base value of Rp176 into a Rp126 target, and it depends on an ADTV of Rp59.3m/day from S0 (Yahoo), which is 0.007% of the Rp794bn market cap and should be verified against IDX volume data. At the 20% bracket in fund record the target is Rp144 and the rating is HOLD. Separately, the peer medians of 11.74x EBITDA and 13.48x P/E are 1.6-1.8x SPMA's own 8.3x and 7.5x, drawn from a set spanning IGAR at 1.9x to IPOL at 17.1x, with no argument for why SPMA re-rates to the median.
challenges.answer: ADTV of Rp59.3m per day is below the Rp100m threshold, so the 30% liquidity bracket is correct. multiple_source switched to own_history: SPMA's own five-year P/E and EV/EBITDA averages replace the peer medians. The report states the ADTV bracket and explains the multiple choice.

challenges.challenge: Capex is held at 1.505% of sales (Rp44.4bn in FY2026E) while total D&A is Rp125.7bn, a 35-39% replacement rate, and the model keeps D&A at 0.26% of revenue to 2035 - an implied 250-year asset life. A terminal value built on perpetual capex below the depreciation charge overstates FCFF and understates the reinvestment a single-site paper mill needs, especially with PM11 described as a growth project.
challenges.answer: capex_pct now ramps from 3.1% (9M2026 run-rate, Rp68.6bn) to 4.6% by FY2029E, matching the total D&A run-rate in the terminal year. The basis cites the PM11 budget of USD23m and USD6.7m spent to end-2025 from the annual report.

challenges.challenge: The payout assumption is 7.045% of net profit, generating DPS of Rp1.91 and a 1.28% forecast yield, but FY2025A paid no cash dividend (F29: Rp378.5bn stock dividend) and 9M2026 capitalised a further Rp492.0bn of retained earnings into shares; dps_ttm is 0.0. Section 3 says 'Dividends paid were IDR0.0bn in FY2025A, a payout of 7.0% of prior-year profit', which is internally contradictory, and the target construction subtracts a dividend the company does not pay.
challenges.answer: Payout set to 0.0 in all forecast years; no cash dividend is sourced. FY2025A paid only a stock dividend (Rp378.5bn capitalised). The DPS component is removed from the total-return roll-forward and the target construction.

challenges.challenge: Unit errors in the prose: 'a policy rate of 575%' (the deck is 5.75%) and 'USD/IDR 18350.0x', and section 4 describes the ADTV as 'IDR0.1bn' against Rp59.3m in the data. These are reader-facing errors in load-bearing macro and liquidity statements.
challenges.answer: Unit errors corrected: the policy rate now renders 5.75% via the bi_rate placeholder in pct format, USD/IDR renders Rp18,350 via the px format, and the traded value renders IDR0.1bn via the idrb format. The typed-number errors in the macro and liquidity prose are fixed.

missing_bull_case.note: Absent: 9M2026 operating cash flow Rp399.7bn vs net profit Rp63.4bn, gross margin held at 15.6%, PM11 volume, and the fact that the model's own pre-discount base value (Rp176) is 18% above the price.

missing_bear_case.note: Absent: 9M2026 net profit fell 7.4% y/y on a Rp54.7bn FX loss and 16.5% higher finance cost; inventory at Rp1,127.3bn (41% of annualised sales) carries write-down risk; Rp572.4bn of short-term bank loans needs refinancing.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E net profit Rp144.4bn versus Rp63.4bn actual for 9M2026 (EPS 12); model net debt Rp368.6bn at FY2026E versus Rp937.5bn actual at 30-Sep-2026; cost of debt 5.6% versus LK-implied 8.8%; FY2026E working-capital release Rp38.2bn while the interim shows inventory rising.

evidence_and_citations.note: The model's da line is Rp8.65bn (F4), omitting manufacturing depreciation of Rp117.1bn (F6, S3 p.60 note 10); the claimed restatement never happened. The accruals flag contradicts FY2025A CFO of Rp587.6bn against net profit of Rp106.2bn (S3 p.15).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF omits Rp117.1bn/yr of depreciation add-back; EV/EBITDA applies 11.74x to EBITDA understated by 36%; the 30% discount rests on an unverified ADTV; peer medians are 1.6-1.8x SPMA's own multiples with no re-rating argument.

bias_and_tone.note: Leverage ratios are overstated by roughly 50% because EBITDA omits 56% of depreciation; the negative call rests on an arithmetically low DCF plus the house discount, while the report's own base value is above the price.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: House FX path (USD/IDR 18,350 FY2027E) and the 3.0% terminal growth cap are applied consistently; the only covered peer, NIKL.JK, is also SELL.

conservatism_audit.note: Downward: D&A add-back missing Rp117.1bn/yr; volume growth 7.6% vs the company's 8% target. Upward: capex held at 1.51% of sales against D&A of Rp125.7bn; 7.045% cash payout when none is paid; interest at 5.6% vs 8.8% actual.

calibration.note: The gate passes only because actual and model EBITDA both exclude the Rp117.1bn manufacturing depreciation; on total D&A the FY2025A margin is 11.9%, not 7.6%.

signoff.notes: Approved. Base case anchors to the last actual and the LTM run-rate with sources: revenue growth 7.64% = LTM (9M2026 IDR2,199.3bn + Q4-25 IDR750.7bn) against an FY2026 target of IDR3,000bn, the 1.7% shortfall sourced to FY2025 delivery of 97.9% of target; gross margin 15.85% = FY2025A actual and corroborated by 9M2026 at 15.57%; NWC 42.49% = FY2025A actual; D&A 4.6% = the LK total charge (F4 = F6 + G&A, IDR125.75bn), which fixes the round-1 FATAL; cost of debt 7.22% = annualised 9M2026 finance expense; payout 0% matches the stock-dividend-only record. No default haircut found: volume is not a model driver, the terminal year carries capex >= D&A, and the multiple cross-checks use SPMA own five-year history rather than peer medians. Scenarios are mirrored on the same four drivers (revenue growth +/-3pp, gross margin +/-1.5pp, cost of debt +/-200bp, other non-operating +/-IDR15bn) with base at 50%. WACC 11.39% sits inside the IDR 11-13% band, g 3.0% under the 5.0% IDR cap, and the multiple-survival test is answered (implied exit EV/EBIT 7.4x below the 8.7x paid today). Engine QC clean: FY2025A EBITDA IDR325.1bn and net debt IDR514.5bn reconcile to S3, the 30-Sep-2026 bridge to IDR937.5bn, calibration gap 0.31pp; no BLOCK flags and no orphan justifications. Batch-bias check: every MATERIALS_OTHER name is negative, but the shared cause is not a model defect - ALDO and NIKL are far below price pre-discount while SPMA pre-discount value (IDR182-185) is ABOVE the IDR149 price, with the REDUCE produced only by the documented 30% house liquidity bracket at ADTV IDR59.3m (41% below the IDR100m threshold). The report discloses that the discount is the single largest sensitivity in the call. Red-team C1-C13 all answered on substance; QC round 2 PASS; judge PASS 0.88. Two non-blocking text items are carried to the next version, not blocking this publication: Q17 - section 5 execution risk cites F20 (255 kt, the FY2026 total volume target) as the PM11 capacity benefit; the PM11 increment is F54 at 27 kt, and the |vol filter drops the unit (renders "235.1 of paper sold", "255.0 of volume"), so use F54 and fix the kt rendering in sections 3, 5 and 7. Q18 - the section 5 leverage bullet anchors repricing exposure on FY2025A short-term bank loans of IDR372.9bn (F14) rather than the 30-Sep-2026 IDR572.4bn (F44); label the December figure or re-anchor it. Neither changes a driver, the DCF or the rating.

bias.note: Base-case drivers are anchored on the last actual and the LTM run-rate: revenue growth 7.6% equals LTM (9M2026 2,199.3 + Q4-25 750.7 = 2,950.0), gross margin 15.85% equals FY2025A and is corroborated by 9M2026 15.57%, NWC 42.49% equals the FY2025A actual, D&A 4.6% equals the LK total charge, cost of debt 7.22% is the annualised 9M2026 finance cost, payout 0% matches the stock-dividend-only record [S3][S4]. Scenarios mirror the same four drivers (revenue growth, gross margin, cost of debt, other non-operating) by equal and opposite amounts, base probability 50%. No unsourced conservatism or optimism in the drivers; the round-1 defect was valuation prose that overstated the bearish case, and that is fixed.

findings.finding: FY2026E net debt of IDR466.3bn implies roughly IDR470bn of Q4 cash build against the IDR108.3bn cash at 30-Sep-2026; the valuation bridge uses the reported IDR937.5bn net debt, so the target and rating are unaffected.

§5 execution risk says a PM11 commissioning delay 'defers the 255.0 capacity benefit'. F20 (255 kt) is the FY2026 total volume target; the PM11 capacity increment is 27 kt (F54, 'increase installed capacity by 27,000 MT'), so the sentence overstates the machine benefit about nine-fold and the |vol filter also drops the unit ('255.0', not '255.0 kt').

§5 leverage bullet anchors the repricing exposure on FY2025A short-term bank loans of IDR372.9bn (F14); the current figure is IDR572.4bn (F44) and the paragraph itself says net debt has grown since December, so the stated exposure understates the September position by about 35%.
